recipes.name: Absolutely the Best Chocolate Chip Cookies

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease 2 cookie sheets.
Cream together butter-flavored shortening, brown sugar, and white sugar in a large bowl until light and fluffy. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition; stir in vanilla.
Combine flour, baking soda, and salt in a separate bowl; gradually stir into creamed mixture.
Fold in chocolate chips until well combined.
Drop by rounded spoonfuls onto the prepared cookie sheets.
Bake in the preheated oven until light brown, 8 to 10 minutes. Allow cookies to cool on the baking sheet for 5 minutes before removing to a wire rack to cool completely.

raw_recipe.headline: Absolutely the Best Chocolate Chip Cookies
raw_recipe.description: These chocolate chip cookies are chewy, crisp, and simple to make with basic pantry staples and Mexican vanilla extract for a spicy, creamy flavor.

review.reviewBody: Great cookie. I'm very strict about using only real butter in all my baking, but I did give butter-flavored shortening a try and was pleasantly surprised. I followed recipe exactly (unsual for me) and it turned out terriffic. I baked mine for 9 min. for the perfect soft and chewy cookie. Of all the cookie recipes I've tried, these taste almost identical to Mrs.Fields coming out of the oven. It also keeps well the day after. TIP - keep the cookies on the cookie sheet for at least 10 min. if you want the cookies to stay moist and soft longer. The natural steam that forms on the bottom penetrates the cookie keeping them moist. A bakery secret.
These are very good but I prefer the Mrs. Fields recipe. It has 1 1/2 cups brown sugar and 1/2 a cup sugar and it gives it a golden quality and a chewy texture. Still very good!!!! Thanks

Yes, this is essentially the Tollhouse recipe, except for the 2 tsp. Mexican vanilla. However, they turned out MUCH better than my Tollhouse cookies ever do. I think it was because of the technique- instead of beating the flour mixture into the creamy mixture (as Tollhouse recipe directs), I followed the recipe and gently folded it in. They were delicious!!! Much fluffier than what I normally get and had a melt in your mouth quality. I highly recommend following the directions as stated in this recipe.

These were good but not great. The first batch came out to mushy and spred way too much. The first thing you need to tell people is are you scooping out the flour or dipping in thus makeing it more compact? After that what I did to fix it is instead of adding more flour I added cocoa powder to make theme cho. choc. chip. These came out fantastick. So If you want to keep them plain dip into the flour bag if not then scoop and add 3/4c. cocoa to the flour mixture. I also upped the vanilla by a bit for more flavor.

Edit..... I've made these about 20 times since and have them down pat. First off, add another tbsp. of flour. Second, add 1/2 tsp. butter flavoring if not using butter flavored shortening. Third, add another 1/2 tsp. Vanilla and up the brown sugar (dark) to 1 cup and white sugar decreased to 1/2 cup then they are perfect. Allow the dough to rest overnight in the refrigerator if possible to get the best flavor.

Cookies were still soft and tasty even after 7 days. Good flavor, easy to make, looked like they came from a bakery. Only changes were 1/4 tsp cream of tartar, used super dark brown sugar, and used dark chocolate disks with extra disks stuck into the dough tops before baking. Will make these again and again.

These are tasty and easy cookies to make. I've made some substitutions to accommodate dietary requirements. I used butter instead of margarine, SweetLeaf Better than Sugar granuals to replace the white sugar and SweetLeaf Brown Better than Sugar granuals, sugar free chocolate chips and homemade vanilla. These changes have not taken away from the taste of these great cookies

I m a new to baking so did lot of worst baking.. Then began to learn about baking science... Spended 1 week to learn about chocochip cookies science.. Dis s d best recipe.. Use 1/2 cup cake flour and 1/2 cup bread flour and no baking soda, it makes cookies flat.. Use baking powder.. 1 tsp..

Awesome recipe! I did sub butter for shortening & put dough in the refrig for about an hour before baking ~ per the oth reviews. It was also recommended to bake for only 8 minutes & I wish that I had noted this & will follow this baking time on my nxt batch. Even w/ the additional baking they were great & my family loved them. Recipe is a keeper!

My go-to recipe! I always use a little bit less salt, use real butter instead of the flavoured shortening, and make them small so there's more to go around. They always disappear within hours of baking!
Make sure that the butter isn't melted when combining with other ingredients, the consistency becomes very liquid and cookies turn out flat and too soft.

Great recipe! I always add extra vanilla extract though and I don't have butter flavored crisco so I just added some butter extract. I also added about a half tsp of baking powder and they turned out amazing. I made a quadruple batch for a bake sale at my son's band performance (very small school) and even though they were the thing we had the most of, they were completely gone before anything else was even half sold. People were coming back for seconds and thirds.

I used shortening then I added some butter. Table spoon or 2. Just used brown sugar. No white. Milk chocolate and dark chocolate chips. Haitian vanilla extract. Rolled dough into plastic wrap like a tube place in fridge
I did 1/2 butter and 1/2 crisco-the crisco flavor came out a little more than the butter. But the consistancy was spot on…didn’t have the butter flavored crisco…

The recipe was horrible. Raw at 10 minutes. Added 5, raw. Added.another 5 and it was burnt. I had to do a second batch, and did 10 minutes it was still raw. I did another 5 minutes, raw on the bottom. I did 17/18 minutes and it was still not even that good then. I will not be repeating this recipe, and I definitely do not recommend.
awesome easy to make my family loved it
My go-to chocolate chip cookie. Been using it for years. Great with any flavor chips or mini chips.

Very easy,a quick recipe utilizing staple ingredients already in the pantry. Using the 1''cookie scoop it made mini cookies about the size of chips ahoy cookies, but you can fit 12 scoops on average cookie sheet. Next time I will double the size of dough scoops.
It was awsome I loved it it was worth the effort
Best cookies exactly what I was craving
I only had butter, and imitation vanilla but this turned out excellent! I made sure the batter was very fluffy before adding in the eggs, vanilla, etc.
As others mentioned, I use 6tsp of regular vanilla.
